newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY SEEN FLAT IN QUIET TRADE, O/N EASE.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY SEEN FLAT IN QUIET TRADE, O/N EASE.

text.p: The Polish zloty was drifting quietly sideways against the basket of currencies in early trade and dealers expected an uneventful day spent on trailing dollar/mark moves on world markets.
"There is nothing happening on the market now and the zloty is likely to trail the dollar/mark rate throughout the day," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.

At 0825 GMT the zloty was at 3.1623/33 against the dollar and 1.8267/72 against the mark, up from 3.1630/40 and down from 1.8255/65 respectively at opening. It was also flat at 2.49/2.46 percent from the parity rate.

On the money market overnight rates eased in early trade by 1.1 point to 20.50/21.90 percent from 21.00/23.00 at opening and some deales said they might ease further during the last day of April's reserve.

Tomorrow/next rates were seen underpinned at 23.10/23.40 percent against 21.0/23.0 percent at opening because they already fell into the new reserve period and banks wanted to keep cash on accounts over the long weekend.
Dealers also said some banks might be searching for cash to pay for T-bills bought on Monday with T/N value date.
